gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: ___ heavy demand, tickets are limited to four per person.
gaps.explanation: 'Owing to + noun' introduces the cause in announcements and notices.

gaps.sentence: ___ the fact that costs had doubled, the project was allowed to continue.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite the fact that' = although, in a more formal wrapper.

gaps.sentence: You can stay up late tonight ___ it's a school night tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless it's a school night' = if it isn't a school night.

gaps.sentence: My sister is terribly reserved, ___ I'll talk to complete strangers.
gaps.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two parallel facts: her nature versus mine.

gaps.sentence: Far from resenting the changes, the staff welcomed them; ___, productivity rose.
gaps.explanation: Rising productivity is an additional point in the same direction: moreover.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: ___ had we sat down than the phone rang.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner' pairs with 'than'; hardly/scarcely pair with 'when'.
